paragraphs: Tavyomi is Mar son of Rav Ashi; see there. In the fool's prophecy, he said that the man who signs Tavyomi would become head; Rav Acha of Difti did not preside: Bava Batra, chapter 1, 12b. Yuchasin, in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, writes that in his days the Persian king Yazdegerd decreed persecutions. Mar bar Rav Ashi prayed, a serpent swallowed the king in his bedchamber, and the persecution ceased. See Yuchasin, sequence of the savoraim, fourth generation. Shalshelet HaKabbalah, 35a, says: “The academy's members appointed Mar son of Rav Ashi head when he was five years old, in his father's honor. He sat thirteen years on his father's throne and died at nineteen in the year 4206 from creation. Because of his tender years, the academy's members called him Rav Tavyomi.” End of quotation. But he already signed his name this way before becoming head! Further, Dorot Olam writes that Meremar became head after Rav Ashi (see there), then Rav Idi (see there), and only after all these did Mar son of Rav Ashi sit on Rav Ashi's throne, in 4215. He presided thirteen years; all his days were good days for Israel, and on this account he was called Rav Tavyomi. He died in 4228; see Yuchasin there. A gloss there, concerning Meremar's becoming head after Rav Ashi, notes that Moed Katan says that Rav Huna bar Natan’s approaching tenure pressed on Rav Ashi’s. Thus Rav Huna bar Natan became academy head after Rav Ashi. However this may be, how could Mar son of Rav Ashi become academy head at five after his father's death? As for “all his days were good, therefore he was called Tavyomi”: he already signed thus before becoming academy head. Chiddushei Aggadot on Bava Batra there raises the same difficulty. Shalshelet HaKabbalah's statement “He died at nineteen” arose because he presided thirteen years and it saw in Dorot Olam that “his days were י״ט.” It understood this as nineteen years of life and therefore inferred that he necessarily became academy head at five. But according to the above, Rav Huna bar Natan, Meremar, and Rav Idi presided after Rav Ashi, followed by Mar son of Rav Ashi. Thus “his days were י״ט” is an abbreviation meaning “good days.” Responsa Rav Sherira Gaon in Yuchasin says he died in 779, equivalent to 4227; Sefer Keritot says 799, equivalent to 4247, on the night following Yom Kippur. The statement that he died in 4206 from creation is a scribal error. See part 1, year 4228. [Glosses: Tavyomi. (a) Bava Metzia 49a, near the end: Rav Tavot; some say his name was Rav Shmuel bar Zutra. Beer Sheva writes that it should read “some say his name was Rav Tavyomi”; so too Chelek 97a and the new Talmud editions. (b) Menachot 70a: Rav Tavyomi bar Kisna should read Tuvi; it was not corrected. Bava Batra 19b: Rabbi Tuvi should read Rav; it was not corrected.]
